# GEO-003 theorem

**Theorem (intrinsic metric of the limiting form).** For a constant positive-definite tensor K and quadratic form `E(f)=int grad f^T K grad f`, the local intrinsic distance generated by the constraint `grad f^T K grad f<=1` is the dual norm `sqrt(delta^T K^-1 delta)`. Hence a graph family can have operator/energy convergence to Euclidean (or anisotropic Riemannian) geometry while its combinatorial shortest-path metric has a different limit.

**Order-of-limits obstruction.** On any fixed finite continuous-time graph, for distinct vertices at jump distance k, `p_t(i,j)=Theta(t^k)` as `t->0`; therefore the continuum-style estimator `sqrt(-4t log p_t(i,j))` tends to zero. A nonzero continuum response distance requires refinement/continuum passage before the small-time limit (with a controlled semigroup/resolvent bridge).
